newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end slightly down, further slide seen.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end slightly down, further slide seen.

text.p: Stocks slid further on Tuesday to close at a new 37-month low despite the government's plan to boost share buying by investment trusts, brokers said.

"The government plan helped boost the market. But fears of worsening fundamentals were more dominant," said Kim Wan-hee, a broker at Dongsuh Securities. The stock index closed 0.48 of a point lower at a provisional 715.97, the lowest since October 9, 1993 when it ended at 712.35.
The finance ministry said on Monday it would allow three Seoul-based investment firms to raise capital by a combined 260 billion won to boost their share buying.
Brokers said the boosting steps were short-lived because the capital increases was not large enough.
"The market looks bottomless. The prospects of any noticeable recovery appears quite slim," said Choo Hee-yup, a broker at Dongwon Securities.
Tightening liquidity due to month-end tax and salary payments was another factor dampening sentiment.
Volume totalled 17.57 million shares, compared with 15.18 million on Monday. Decliners outpaced advancers 443 to 376 with 193 unchanged.

Brokers said the government's plan to sell 360 billion won worth of Korea Telecom shares this week and list the state-run company in the first half of 1997 was in the centre of fears over a stock oversupply.
The annual APEC conference, which has just ended in Manila, hardly affected the market, brokers said.
"Who cares about what's happening in Manila? What investors need is more direct factors that can boost the market," Choo of Dongwon said.
